lab_table.hypothesis: Shrinking pasted defects into the missed size band (0.3-0.7x source size) will raise recall on small instances, especially inclusion. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 jumps and small-tertile recall improves relative to C2 and control.
Allocation alone (more inclusion images at normal scale) improves inclusion AP. If C2 ~= C1, scale is irrelevant and allocation is the lever; if C2 < C1, small-scale pasting is the key factor.

Pasting defects onto cross-class backgrounds (any_class) increases background/contrast diversity and helps the low-contrast misses (patches low-contrast recall 0.21) without hurting. Confirmed if C3 beats the balanced default-scale control on mAP or worst-class AP.
CONTROL (added by the lab): default generation recipe, balanced allocation.

lesson: Small-scale pastes (0.3-0.7x source size) are the key lever: they lifted inclusion AP by +0.25 and mAP50 by +0.12, far beyond what allocation alone achieved (C2). Cross-class (any_class) backgrounds hurt patches, so keep same_class. Next: push scale toward the floor (0.3-0.5) and/or prefer_small sources to target the smallest missed inclusions, while keeping inclusion-heavy allocation.
